1. Executive Summary

The Omnichannel Retail POS and Inventory Management System addresses a critical gap in the digitizing retail landscape: fragmented legacy software that causes inventory inaccuracies, stockouts, and poor performance under load. This platform will serve as the core Offline-to-Online Transformation package for traditional retail enterprises.

The system will unify physical and digital retail operations into a single source of truth — processing transactions with high throughput, maintaining real-time inventory parity across geographic nodes, and delivering actionable business intelligence through a centralized dashboard.
2. Problem Statement
Multi-location retailers scaling their operations face compounding systemic failures:
Severe latency under large datasets causes inaccurate inventory synchronization across brick-and-mortar stores, warehouses, and online storefronts.
Disconnected systems force manual workflows, resulting in stockouts, overselling, and inconsistent pricing.
Conventional POS platforms degrade in performance as databases grow with historical transactions and catalog records.
No single system provides unified visibility across all sales channels in real time.
3. Goals & Non-Goals
3.1 Goals
Architect a cloud-native, omnichannel POS and Inventory Management System.
Achieve sub-second inventory synchronization across all connected sales channels post-transaction.
Eliminate data discrepancies between physical stock and digital records via ACID-compliant transactions.
Provide real-time business intelligence through a centralized analytics dashboard.
Maintain high availability and support offline POS operation with seamless re-sync on reconnection.
3.2 Non-Goals
This system will not build a consumer-facing e-commerce storefront (only the backend POS and inventory engine).
Native mobile applications are out of scope; the frontend is web-based and responsive.
Full ERP integration (payroll, HR) is not included in the MVP.
Third-party marketplace integrations (Amazon, Flipkart) are deferred to post-MVP.

6. MVP Feature Specifications
The following modules constitute the Minimum Viable Product. All features below are required for a passing evaluation.
6.1 Unified Product Catalog
Core Module
A centralized Product Information Management (PIM) system that serves as the foundation for all inventory and sales operations.
Multi-variant item support: distinguish items by size, color, and SKU within a single product record.
Hierarchical categorization with parent/child category relationships.
Rule-based dynamic pricing engine with scheduled promotional overrides.
Full-text search and cursor-based pagination for catalog browsing at scale.
Redis caching for frequently accessed catalog data with intelligent cache invalidation on price/stock updates.
6.2 Omnichannel Order Management
Core Module
The central routing engine that aggregates orders from all sales channels and optimizes fulfillment.
Ingest orders from physical POS terminals and digital storefronts through a unified order API.
Algorithmic fulfillment center selection based on mathematical optimization of geographic proximity and localized stock availability.
Order lifecycle management: Pending → Processing → Fulfilled → Refunded state machine.
ACID-compliant order creation: stock decrement, financial ledger update, and order record creation succeed or fail as a single atomic transaction.
6.3 Real-Time POS Terminal
Core Module
A web-based register interface engineered for high-velocity retail environments.
Keyboard shortcut support and barcode-simulated product search for rapid item addition.
Client-side cart calculation engine: aggregate unit prices, apply dynamic discount matrices, compute localized tax rates.
Multi-modal payment integration: cash, credit/debit card, and digital wallets.
Offline-first capability: local cart state persists through network interruption and syncs atomically on reconnection.
Optimistic UI updates with rollback on transaction failure for perceived speed.
6.4 Automated Inventory Engine
Core Module
The tracking module responsible for real-time stock accuracy and proactive replenishment.
Atomic stock decrement on every order confirmation using MongoDB multi-document transactions.
Real-time stock visibility dashboard across all geographic nodes.
Basic sales velocity forecasting algorithm to predict reorder points.
Automated low-stock alerts with configurable threshold rules per SKU and store.
Inter-store transfer workflow: initiate, approve, and reconcile stock movements between warehouses.
6.5 Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
Security Module
A stateless, JWT-based authentication and authorization system with strict role segregation.
Three role tiers: Cashier, Inventory Manager, System Administrator — each with isolated permission sets.
bcrypt password hashing for all stored credentials.
JWT access tokens with configurable expiration and refresh token rotation.
RBAC middleware protecting all API routes with role-level enforcement.
7. Architecture & Technology Stack
The system follows a decoupled, headless architecture isolating the frontend presentation layer from backend business logic. This ensures independent scaling and maximum maintainability.
Component
Technology
Architectural Rationale
Frontend Application
React.js, Tailwind CSS
Dynamic, component-driven UI with responsive POS interfaces adaptable across tablet and desktop hardware profiles.
Backend Services
Node.js, Express.js, TypeScript
Highly concurrent async runtime for I/O-heavy operations and real-time transaction processing. TypeScript enforces compile-time type safety.
Primary Database
MongoDB via Mongoose ODM
Flexible NoSQL document structure for variable retail schemas. Mongoose provides structured ODM with cascading deletion and indexing support.
Caching Layer
Redis
In-memory data structure store to reduce database read loads for product catalogs and active promotional rules.
State Management
Redux Toolkit / Zustand
Manages active POS cart, authenticated user session, and offline/online network status detection for resilient operations.
Testing
Vitest / Jest, Cypress / Playwright
Unit tests for critical business logic; E2E tests for concurrent transaction simulation and race condition detection.
Deployment Pipeline
Docker, Vercel/AWS, GitHub Actions
Environment parity via containerization. CI/CD pipelines automate linting, type-checking, testing, and deployment.

8. Four-Week Sprint Roadmap

The project is strictly divided into four weekly sprints. Daily commits to GitHub are mandatory for evaluation eligibility. A compressed or monolithic commit history will result in immediate disqualification.
Sprint 1
System Architecture, Schema Design & Authentication
Initialize GitHub monorepo with branch protection rules (PR reviews required before merge to main).
Containerize local development environment using Docker — provision MongoDB and Redis instances.
Design and implement all six Mongoose schemas (Users, Stores, Products, Inventory Ledgers, Orders, Order Line Items) with explicit indexing strategies.
Implement stateless JWT authentication with bcrypt password hashing.
Build RBAC middleware differentiating Cashier, Manager, and System Administrator permissions.
Deliverable: Fully secured, running backend with authentication endpoints and validated schema structure.
Sprint 2
Core API Development & Inventory Logic
Build full CRUD RESTful API for the Product Catalog with cursor-based pagination.
Implement MongoDB full-text search and advanced filtering for the product catalog.
Construct the core Inventory Engine transaction endpoint using MongoDB multi-document ACID transactions (stock decrement + financial ledger update + order creation in one atomic unit).
Integrate Redis caching for product catalog with intelligent cache invalidation on price/stock changes.
Write unit tests using Vitest or Jest for all critical transaction logic paths.
Deliverable: All backend APIs functional and unit-tested; Redis caching active.
Sprint 3
Frontend Integration & POS Interface
Initialize React.js frontend with global state management (Redux Toolkit or Zustand).
State manager must handle: active cart state, authenticated user session, and offline/online network detection.
Build the POS terminal UI with keyboard shortcut support and barcode-simulated search.
Implement client-side cart calculation: unit price aggregation, dynamic discount matrices, localized tax calculation.
Wire all frontend components to Week 2 backend APIs with robust error handling and optimistic UI updates.
Ensure full responsive design using Tailwind CSS for cross-device compatibility.
Deliverable: Fully functional POS terminal UI connected to backend APIs.
Sprint 4
Stabilization, Testing & Deployment Pipeline
Conduct comprehensive E2E testing using Cypress or Playwright — simulate concurrent cashier transactions, actively test for race conditions and database deadlocks.
Finalize GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline: linting → type-checking → full unit test suite on every PR.
Deploy frontend to Vercel and containerized backend to AWS or Render.
Generate comprehensive API documentation using Swagger or OpenAPI.
Write a detailed README: environment setup steps, architectural decisions, schema diagrams, and seed data instructions.
Verify daily commit history spans all 4 weeks — submission will be disqualified otherwise.
Deliverable: Production-deployed application with full documentation and CI/CD active.

10. Security Requirements
The following security controls are non-negotiable and subject to automated scanning:
All API endpoints require valid JWT authentication; public routes limited to /auth/register and /auth/login.
Passwords must be hashed using bcrypt with a minimum cost factor of 12.
Environment variables (DB URI, JWT secret, Redis URL, API keys) must never be committed to the repository — use GitHub Secrets.
GITHUB_TOKEN permissions in workflow files must be scoped to read-only unless a deployment task explicitly requires write access.
Input validation must be applied to all POST/PUT endpoints to prevent injection attacks.
HTTP security headers (CORS policy, helmet.js) must be configured on the Express backend.

12. Open Questions & Assumptions
Assumptions
Interns have access to a cloud MongoDB Atlas cluster or can run MongoDB locally via Docker.
A free-tier Vercel account and AWS/Render account are available for deployment.
Payment gateway integration uses simulated/mock responses; no real financial processing is required in the MVP.
The barcode scanning feature is simulated via keyboard input; no physical scanner hardware is required.
Open Questions
Should inter-store stock transfers require manager approval before execution, or are they immediate?
What is the retention period for completed order records in the primary database before archival?
Will the predictive reorder algorithm need to account for seasonal demand variation in the MVP, or is a simple moving average sufficient?
What is the maximum number of concurrent cashier sessions the system must support in a load test scenario?
